description: A stereo recording buffer read by up to four playheads at once, so it works as a tap delay, a chorus, a reverse or granular effect, or an oscillator

params.text: Sets how long the buffer is, from a tenth of a second fully left to 10 seconds fully right; with a cable at CLOCK it multiplies or divides the clocked length instead
Attenuverts the DELAY input before it is added to the DELAY knob
Chooses what the playhead controls mean: Phase is the distance behind the writing head, Phase beat is the position in the buffer itself, Speed is how fast it runs, and Grain restarts it as a grain
Chooses how the playheads reach the outputs: Stereo mixes them, Stereo poly gives each its own channel, Stereo spread runs first left to last right, and ping-pong runs left to right and back
Sets where the playheads read, as a fraction of the buffer
Attenuverts the first PHASE input before it is added to the PHASE knob
Attenuverts the second PHASE input before it is added to the PHASE knob
Sets how fast the playheads read the buffer, in octaves from -4 to +4 either side of the recorded speed
Attenuverts the first SPEED input before it is added to the SPEED knob
Attenuverts the second SPEED input before it is added to the SPEED knob
Runs the playheads backwards through the buffer
Chooses how much of the speed is quantised to whole octaves: None, Knob, Knob and the first input, or All
Limits how fast the playhead speed is allowed to change, so a jump in speed becomes a glide
Sets how long each grain lasts in Grain mode, from a tenth of a second fully left to 2 seconds fully right
Attenuverts the first GRAIN input before it is added to the GRAIN knob
Attenuverts the second GRAIN input before it is added to the GRAIN knob
Sets the level of every playhead
Attenuverts the first LEVEL input before it is added to the LEVEL knob
Attenuverts the second LEVEL input before it is added to the LEVEL knob
Sets how strongly a playhead's level is shaped by where in the buffer it is reading
Attenuverts the input below it before it is added to the shape force knob
Sets the shape the levels follow across the buffer, from a falling ramp through a triangle to a rising ramp
Attenuverts the input below it before it is added to the shape wave knob
Sets the level the input is recorded into the buffer at, silence fully left and twice the input fully right
Attenuverts the IN input before it is added to the IN knob
Sets the level the playheads are read out at, silence fully left and twice their level fully right
Attenuverts the OUT input before it is added to the OUT knob
Blends the dry input against the playheads, the input alone fully left and the playheads alone fully right
Attenuverts the MIX input before it is added to the MIX knob
Narrows the stretch of buffer the level shape is spread over, leaving the rest of it silent
Sets how sharply each grain fades in and out at its ends

The right input; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
Shifts the buffer length, 5V covering the whole of the DELAY knob's travel at full attenuverter
Sets the buffer length from the time between rising edges here, times the pulses per beat chosen on the menu, then multiplied or divided by the DELAY knob; the result is held at 10 seconds at most
Moves the playheads through the buffer, 10V a whole buffer at full attenuverter; a polyphonic cable here gives one playhead per channel
Moves the playheads through the buffer, 10V a whole buffer at full attenuverter; a polyphonic cable here gives one playhead per channel
Sets the playback speed at a volt an octave, scaled by the attenuverter beside it; a polyphonic cable here gives one playhead per channel
Sets the playback speed at a volt an octave, scaled by the attenuverter beside it; a polyphonic cable here gives one playhead per channel
Runs a playhead backwards while the voltage on its channel is above 0V
Shifts the grain length, 10V covering the whole of the GRAIN knob's travel at full attenuverter
Shifts the grain length, 10V covering the whole of the GRAIN knob's travel at full attenuverter
Sets the level of a playhead, 10V full and 0V silent at full attenuverter; a polyphonic cable here gives each playhead its own level
Sets the level of a playhead, 10V full and 0V silent at full attenuverter; a polyphonic cable here gives each playhead its own level
Shifts how strongly the position shaping is applied, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel at full attenuverter
Shifts the shape the levels follow across the buffer, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel at full attenuverter
Shifts the recording level, 10V covering the whole of the IN knob's travel at full attenuverter; the total is held between silence and twice the input
Shifts the output level, 10V covering the whole of the OUT knob's travel at full attenuverter; the total is held between silence and twice the level
Shifts the blend, 10V covering the whole of the MIX knob's travel at full attenuverter; the total is held between the two ends
A rising edge puts the writing position back to the start of the buffer; it is read in Phase beat mode only

outputs.text: The left output: the playheads mixed and scaled by the OUT knob, then blended against the dry input by MIX
The right output: the playheads mixed and scaled by the OUT knob, then blended against the dry input by MIX

notes: nothing is heard until audio is patched into IN; the buffer starts as silence and only holds what has been recorded into it.
the playhead count is the channel count of the cable on whichever jacks the mode reads: PHASE in the two phase modes, SPEED in speed mode, any of the three in grain mode.
with nothing patched to those jacks the module runs one playhead, and it never runs more than sixteen.
the buffer holds 10 seconds at 48kHz and the delay time is worked out against that rate rather than the engine's, so at another engine rate the delay is not the number of seconds shown.
the buffer display is a single widget, so nothing drawn on it can be clicked for help.
menu: Mode HD — reads the buffer with interpolation for a cleaner sound; turning it off gives lo-fi artefacts
Mode anti-click — fades the output over a few samples when a playhead jumps, to take out the click
Clock PPQN: 1, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 96 — sets how many rising edges at CLOCK make up one beat of buffer length
